quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone starts here.
Railroad crossing ahead.
School zone ahead.
Construction work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs show construction, maintenance, or emergency work ahead.

questions.question: How can you make sure your health does not make you an unsafe driver?

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and get regular checkups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Only drive within what your body can handle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits, understand how medicines affect you, and stay in good health. Only drive if it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: What happens when a driver goes much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: They are always a very safe driver.
They always have the right-of-way.
They should not allow cars behind them to pass.
They can create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be unsafe. If traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let other cars pass. Only drive slowly when conditions require it.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another car?

options.text: Next to a solid yellow line.
On a hill or around a curve.
When cars are coming toward you.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass when it could be dangerous. Avoid passing in no passing zones, where you cannot see ahead clearly, or when oncoming cars are near.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When passing on a highway with multiple lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for cars coming toward you.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: If a green turn arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You can no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green turn arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: An adult can safely hold them.
They are safe standing on the floor in the back.
They will not get hurt in a crash because they are small.
They must always be properly secured in a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must always be properly secured in a seat.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use proper safety seats for children.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is driving aggressively?

options.text: Avoid looking at them, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow closely behind them.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at them, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is being dangerous, stay calm and create distance. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. Before you start moving, you should:

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and check behind your car. Do not rely only on your mirrors. This is especially important when children are nearby.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, drive:

options.text: Through shallow water.
More quickly.
More slowly.
Through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving more slowly reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive no differently than normal.
Can drive faster because they are more alert.
Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Your mind becomes focused on other things. Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.

questions.question: Most warning signs are:

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: You may turn right on red:

options.text: After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles.
Before pedestrians have crossed any crosswalks.
Where there is a sign prohibiting turning right on red.
Before coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on red after a full stop if it is safe and if there is no sign against it. Always watch for pedestrians crossing in front of you.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs have an eight-sided shape called an octagon. This unique shape is used only for stop signs.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle arrives at your right at the same time, you must yield to that vehicle. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: At high speeds, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers to avoid them.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop and block the emergency vehicle from passing.
Clear a path for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clear a path for the emergency vehicle to pass.
questions.explanation: Give emergency vehicles with flashing lights a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the bridge ahead.
The bridge is one-way only.
Only one car can use the bridge at a time.
The bridge may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck safely.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You must go slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then go when the way is clear.
You must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. You cannot go until the light changes to green or a green arrow appears.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a break every two hours on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over in a safe place to nap or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will not roll into traffic.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually slows your reaction to hazards.
Usually makes you drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving slows how fast you react to traffic and hazards. It is always unsafe.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you a lane is ending. Prepare to merge safely.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Accelerate to avoid a red light.
Continue driving, as you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, create a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a work zone with a "45 mph where workers present" sign, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down immediately.
Drive safely for conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present.
Merge to the right lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely for conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present.
questions.explanation: In work zones with an advisory speed for workers, slow down when workers are present but you may drive at the normal speed limit when no workers are present. Watch for workers and adjust your speed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway ends.
A one-way street begins.
A one-way street ends.
A divided highway begins.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway begins.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead is a divided highway. Keep to the right of the divider.

questions.question: When visibility decreases, what should be your first action?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed first when visibility decreases or conditions become dangerous.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: While backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in condominium complexes if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 25 mph
35 mph
45 mph
55 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in condominium complexes is 25 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions they give over their loudspeaker. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren or air horn but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph could take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers take much longer to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need almost 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
Upcoming hill.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming hill.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you that a steep hill is ahead and you should be ready to adjust your speed for safe driving.

questions.question: You are waiting in a line at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through with no cross traffic, what should you do?

options.text: You may proceed through the intersection without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the vehicle directly ahead of you without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip stopping just because other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely into traffic when it is safe to do so.
